scenario: Your manager hands you this slide in the meeting.
passage: Q3 Sales Update | Sales up 12% | Two new regions opened | Churn down to 3%
question: What do you say first?
option_0: Good news: sales grew 12% this quarter, driven by two new regions.
option_1: Um, I have not seen this slide, so I will just read it out.
option_2: This slide says Q3 Sales Update. Next bullet: sales up 12%.
option_3: Sorry, I was not prepared for this.
explanation: Lead with the key message and its cause. Reading the slide or apologising wastes the first ten seconds.

scenario: A colleague is ill and you present their slide.
passage: Support Load | Tickets up 40% | Hires frozen | CSAT still 91% | Backlog 310
question: What do you say first?
option_0: Our support team is absorbing 40% more tickets with no new hires, and quality is holding.
option_1: Let me start with the backlog, which is 310 tickets.
option_2: As you can see, there are many numbers on this slide.
option_3: I think this slide is about support, maybe.
explanation: Join the bullets into one message before going into detail. The others start with a detail, a filler or a hedge.

scenario: You are asked to present this slide cold.
passage: Team Offsite | Book venue by May | Budget 4,000 | 18 people
question: What do you say first?
option_0: Sorry, I have not seen this, so I will read each line.
option_1: We need to book the offsite venue by May for 18 people, within a 4,000 budget.
option_2: Um, so this is about an offsite, I think.
option_3: The title says Team Offsite and below it are three bullets.
explanation: Join the bullets into one message the audience can act on. The others apologise, hedge or describe the slide.

scenario: Your director asks you to cover the risk slide.
passage: Launch Risks | Vendor delay 2 weeks | Test coverage 70% | No rollback plan
question: What do you say first?
option_0: Honestly there are a lot of risks and I am not sure which matter.
option_1: Let me go through the three bullets from the top, one at a time.
option_2: The launch has no rollback plan, and the vendor delay adds two weeks of risk.
option_3: Test coverage is 70%, which is probably fine, so I will skip ahead.
explanation: Lead with the most serious message and tie it to the slide. The others hedge, read in order or dismiss a risk.

scenario: A colleague forgot to attach notes to this slide.
passage: Hiring Plan | 6 roles open | 2 offers out | Start date 1 June
question: What do you say first?
option_0: I do not have the notes, so I cannot say much about this.
option_1: Hiring plan. Six roles open. Two offers out. Start date 1 June.
option_2: As you can see, hiring is going on and there are some roles.
option_3: Six roles are open, two offers are out, and the start date is 1 June.
explanation: One joined sentence with all three facts gives a clear message. The others apologise, read the bullets or stay vague.

scenario: The CEO joins the call as you start presenting.
passage: Churn Review | Churn 3% to 5% | Price rise in April | Two enterprise accounts left
question: What do you say first?
option_0: Sorry, I did not expect the CEO, so please bear with me.
option_1: Churn rose from 3% to 5% after the April price rise, and two enterprise accounts left.
option_2: Let me start at the top and read each bullet, if that is okay.
option_3: There are a few things to look at here, and some of them matter.
explanation: Open with the headline and its cause, even with a senior listener. The others apologise, read aloud or stay vague.
